author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: pm stats default output is dominated by rows that carry no information: 7 of 17 type buckets are zero, the status split agents actually need is missing, and the row contract costs more than the data

Measured on the live 2429-item tracker: the default TOON output is 745 bytes, of which the row_contract block is 285 bytes (38 percent). by_type zero-fills every registered type, so 7 of 17 rows report 0 - Card, Changeset, Event, Meeting, TwinAsset, TwinFacility and VcsRef - registered by the bundled exemplar extensions (kanban-profile, digital-twin-exemplar, vcs-exemplar) and by builtins this workspace does not use. by_status zero-fills 3 of 6. Meanwhile the question an agent actually asks, how many items of each type are open versus closed, is not answerable from stats at all and needs a second command (pm aggregate --group-by type --completion). Reshaping the default to drop zero rows, fold the lifecycle split into by_type and drop the row contract yields 468 bytes, 37 percent smaller while strictly more informative. Zero-fill is currently documented as intentional in docs/COMMANDS.md, so this is a declared default change rather than a bug fix. Risk to manage: by_type moves from a flat count map to a lifecycle-bucketed shape, so any downstream reader treating by_type values as numbers breaks; the opt-in restore flag and a contracts-snapshot update in the same change are the mitigation.

Default pm stats omits every by_type and by_status row whose count is zero and reports the omitted bucket count as a scalar so the information is not lost; by_type carries the lifecycle split per type (total plus open, in_progress, blocked, draft, closed, canceled, other) derived from the groupItemsByDimension primitive that already serves --by-assignee, with no second traversal of the item set; An explicit opt-in flag restores the zero-filled distribution for governance dashboards that need unused states visible; Default pm stats emits no row contract block, and the reshaped default is added to the token-budget-gate corpus with a declared ceiling so the saving is enforced rather than observed once; docs/COMMANDS.md drops the zero-fill-is-a-feature claim and the contracts snapshot, completion scripts and MCP surface are regenerated in the same change

message: Filed from a measured read of pm stats default output on the live tracker

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Measurement and implementation map, taken on the live 2429-item tracker at 2026-08-11.

Measured today
- pm stats default TOON 745 bytes, --json 957 bytes. The row_contract block is 285 bytes, 38 percent of the default.
- by_type emits 17 rows, 7 of them zero: Card, Changeset, Event, Meeting, TwinAsset, TwinFacility, VcsRef.
- by_status emits 6 rows, 3 of them zero: draft, in_progress, blocked.
- Non-zero types are Issue 820, Task 660, Feature 423, Chore 289, Epic 89, Decision 64, Story 53, Plan 23, Milestone 7, Reminder 1.
- A reshaped default carrying the same totals plus a per-type lifecycle split, minus zero rows and minus the row contract, renders at 468 bytes: 37 percent smaller and strictly more informative.

Where the zero rows come from
Not from workspace configuration. settings item_types definitions is empty and the workspace schema block is empty. pm schema list reports 17 types as 11 builtin, 1 custom, 5 extension. Event and Meeting are builtin and unused here. Story is the one custom type and is in active use with 53 items, so a rule that hides non-builtin types would hide a type this project uses - the correct rule is to hide empty buckets, not foreign ones. Card comes from the bundled kanban-profile extension, TwinAsset and TwinFacility from digital-twin-exemplar, Changeset and VcsRef from vcs-exemplar; all three are bundled builtin extension directories that load without being installed.

Implementation map
- The zero-fill originates in zeroByType and zeroByStatus in the stats module, which pre-seed a bucket for every registry entry before counting.
- The lifecycle split needs no new logic: groupItemsByDimension in the metadata-coverage module already accepts a type dimension and returns lifecycle-bucketed rows. It is the same primitive that serves --by-assignee, --by-tag and --by-priority, and stats already builds the classifier it needs.
- The row contract for stats is declared in the read-output projection table as row_keys by_type and by_status. Changing the shape of by_type without updating that declaration would leave the published jq selector pointing at a shape that no longer exists.
- The zero-fill is documented as deliberate in docs/COMMANDS.md and that sentence has to go in the same change.
- The stats default is absent from the token-budget-gate corpus, which currently carries an activity-default entry but no stats entry. Adding one is what turns the saving into an enforced ceiling.

Cross-check
pm aggregate --group-by type --completion already answers the per-type lifecycle question, at roughly 1.5 kB and as a second invocation. Folding it into the stats default removes one round trip from every orientation sequence rather than adding a surface.
